note: Curated from the Btown Brief newsletter vault (editions Sep 21 - Oct 19, 2026, after an extended gap since the Aug 28 refresh — every prior point had aged past the six-week cap, so the file was rebuilt fresh). TALKING-POINTS.md is the style doctrine; refreshes land as PRs and points age out via 'added'.

points.text: Omron, a Japanese automation giant, is buying South Burlington's OnLogic for $675 million — the computer hardware maker that Roland and Lisa Groeneveld started at their kitchen table in 2003 keeps its name, leadership and local jobs, and every employee gets a $1,500-a-month-worked bonus, up to $90,000 for a five-year employee. What would you do with a surprise $90,000 bonus?

Burlington's Mexican food scene just grew in two unlikely spots: Doña Esa now serves home-style dishes like mole rosa, tinted pink with beets and hibiscus, inside Pine Street's Doma Bar, while Taquería Don Richard built a TikTok following on handmade tortilla tacos out of the University Mall food court. Tacos from the food court, or dinner in a bar's living room — which wins your Friday night?

Burlyaxe Throwing closed its North Winooski Avenue space after seven years and, in its own words, hundreds of thousands of axes thrown — though the mobile trailer is still booking events. What's the most surprising thing you've thrown at a target for fun?

Colchester High sophomore Juliet Wager became the first girl in her troop to reach Eagle Scout, building the 'Snack and Books' pantry near Mallets Bay School, a Little Free Library stocked with canned goods and books for anyone who'd rather not sign up for a food shelf. What's a project you'd build for your own neighborhood?

Nectar's on Main Street could come back to life — Shawn Cliche has filed plans to fill all three floors with food, live music, DJs and pool tables, though he says it's still undecided whether the Nectar's name sticks around. What would you name it, if not Nectar's?

Natural Nest Play Café opened on Shelburne Road this month, a Montessori-style space stocked with all-natural toys where caregivers can sip coffee while kids up to age 8 play — the first franchise location of the Delaware-based chain outside Delaware. What's the toy you'd never grow out of playing with there?

The 115-room Sugar House Hotel opened October 21st in Winooski, with a rooftop restaurant overlooking a 100-acre nature preserve and a complimentary maple creemee for every guest at check-in. What would be your excuse to check in?

GlobalFoundries switched on a new battery storage system at its Essex Junction campus — at 16 megawatts, the largest battery ever installed in Vermont — paired with solar panels covering 30 acres of old parking lot and brownfield. What's the next 'biggest in Vermont' thing you'd want to see built?

WJOY, the AM station broadcasting from South Burlington since 1967, just marked 80 years on the air by inviting longtime listeners in to reminisce. What's the station or show you grew up with on the dial?

19-year-old Mustafa Khudaier reopened the food kiosk at Church and College streets as Sabah's House, serving his mother Sabah's $14 chicken shawarma recipe to an already loyal following. What's the one dish you'd walk across town for?

The gunboat Philadelphia, the country's oldest surviving warship, has sat at the bottom of Lake Champlain since the Revolutionary War's 1776 Battle of Valcour Island — raised in 1935, it's now getting a $1.7 million cleaning and conservation effort as the battle marks its 250th anniversary. What do you think is still waiting to be found on the bottom of the lake?

Big Heavy World is handing its 29-year music archive over to the Vermont Historical Society, including the actual ladle from Nectar's and the door from 242 Main. What piece of a long-gone Burlington spot would you want to see in a museum case?

Bridge No. 150, the 359-foot span over the Winooski River built in 1928, is listed free on Vermont's Craigslist — federal rules require VTrans to offer historic bridges away before tearing them down, and so far the only reply has asked, 'Can I move it tomorrow?' What would you actually do with a free 98-year-old bridge?

Vermont scientists are gluing tiny solar-powered trackers onto monarch butterflies and following named ones like Ann, Scott and Pam in real time as they migrate — some, it turns out, winter in Florida instead of Mexico. Which name would you give a monarch you spotted in your own yard?

Winooski just finished its $28.3 million Main Street overhaul, two years in the making, with a new bike lane, more than 200 new plants and trees, and the utility lines finally buried underground. What's the first thing you'll do on the new strip?
The Mockingbird Foundation, started by Phish fans back in 1996, launched a new scholarship this fall for Vermont college students studying music. Which local musician do you think deserves it most?

A visitor from Edmonton wore the same pair of Darn Tough socks for 101 days straight without washing them, smashing the old company record of 55 — he says the merino wool never stank. What's the longest you've gone wearing or using one single thing before giving in and washing it?

Hey June, a stationery shop and letterpress studio in Richmond, joined the international Sunday Letter Project this summer — write to the shop and a stranger there writes you back, with mail already arriving from as far as England and Australia. Who's the stranger you'd want to send a letter to?

A Reddit thread asking for Burlington's best breakfast spot turned into a 105-comment ranking — Sneakers Bistro came out on top, Henry's Diner took a close second right as it marked 100 years in business, and Deep City wasn't far behind, staffed by the old Penny Cluse crew. Which of the three gets your order this weekend?

Breeze Airways is adding Burlington flights to Myrtle Beach and Fort Lauderdale starting next May, and the airport is already teasing a new warm-weather international destination to be announced by the end of October. What international spot are you hoping they fly to next?
